name: wooden dock crane with pulley and hanging cargo net
label: pirate-isles/pi-dock-crane

answer.main_body: crane mast and horizontal jib arm
answer.evidence: The crane mast cap and horizontal beam top are drawn in flat side elevation without foreshortened top surfaces (the mast cap is a flat outline at row 3 with 0px top, and the horizontal beam top is at most a 1px highlight). Although the base plinth and hanging cargo show top planes, the main crane structure lacks top surfaces.

Both the substantial base box (rows 36-41, 6px top surface) and the suspended cargo box (rows 27-31, 5px top surface) clearly display foreshortened top surfaces consistent with 3/4 top-down perspective.

answer.main_body: wooden crane mast and jib arm
answer.evidence: The crane mast and horizontal jib beam are drawn in a flat side elevation. The horizontal beam extending to the right shows no foreshortened top surface (only a 1px line between outlines), and the mast cap has no visible top, failing the requirement that beam tops and horizontal surfaces must be visible from above in 3/4 view.

answer.main_body: crane mast and horizontal boom arm
answer.evidence: The main body of the crane (vertical mast and horizontal boom arm) is drawn as a flat 2D side elevation. The horizontal beam has no visible top surface, and the mast cap is just a flat 1px outline. The base plinth cannot be credited as the main body.
